games.title: Nuts & Milk
games.note: Hudson Soft's single-screen fruit-gathering platformer—the first third-party cartridge ever published for Nintendo's Famicom, complete with a built-in stage editor and later ubiquitous on Dendy multicarts.

games.title: Circus Charlie
games.note: Six cheerful circus events—leaping through flaming rings atop a lion, monkey-dodging on a tightrope, trampolines, rolling balls, horseback hurdles, and flying trapeze—stapled onto almost every 1990s Dendy multicart.

games.title: Battle City
games.note: Two-player top-down tank co-op built around guarding a brick-walled Eagle base, grabbing star upgrades, and building custom arenas in an early console level editor—beloved across post-Soviet & Eastern European living rooms on Dendy simply as 'Tanki'.

games.title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III: The Manhattan Project
games.note: Konami's original 8-bit co-op brawler—giving each Turtle a signature health-spending special attack after Shredder lifts Manhattan into the sky—cherished on NES and yellow Dendy cartridges alike.

games.title: Darkwing Duck
games.note: Built by Capcom on its NES Mega Man engine, pairing nonlinear boss stages across St. Canard with cape shot-deflection, gas-gun ammo switching, and hanging from overhead hooks—an unmistakable 1990s Dendy favorite.

games.title: Felix the Cat
games.note: Late-era 8-bit cartoon platformer from Hudson Soft where collecting Magic Bag hearts upgraded Felix step-by-step from a boxing glove into a wizard, car, tank, submarine, or airplane.

games.title: Battletoads & Double Dragon
games.note: Rare's crossover brawler teaming Rash, Zitz, and Pimple with Billy and Jimmy Lee across colossal spacecraft, speeder bikes, and zero-gravity stages—pushing 8-bit hardware to its absolute limit.

links.took: Top-down brick-maze tank combat centered on protecting a walled Eagle headquarters from waves of enemy armor
links.added: Simultaneous two-player co-op defense, star power-ups that chewed through steel walls, terrain hazards, and a built-in custom map editor right on the cartridge

links.took: Capcom's crisp NES run-and-gun physics, selectable boss-stage structure, and expressive 8-bit sprite craft
links.added: Hanging and dropping from overhead hooks, blocking projectiles with Darkwing's cape, and swapping specialized gas-gun ammo mid-stage

links.took: Hudson Soft's brisk 8-bit side-scrolling momentum, collectible stage tokens, and lighthearted world variety
links.added: Multi-tier Magic Bag vehicle transformations—stepping up to a car, tank, airplane, or dolphin submarine as you gathered hearts without taking damage

links.took: Two-player 8-bit belt-scrolling co-op brawling tuned around two-button Famicom and NES pads
links.added: Four distinct Turtles with unique weapon reach and signature crowd-clearing throws that spent a sliver of health

links.took: Rare's oversized smash-hit finishers, vehicle-stage variety, and two-player co-op spectacle
links.added: Playable Double Dragon martial artists Billy and Jimmy Lee alongside all three Toads, with a more approachable difficulty curve and ship-boarding stages

links.took: Technōs Japan's street-brawling brothers Billy and Jimmy Lee, spin kicks, and Shadow Boss
links.added: Blended Double Dragon's martial-arts moveset directly into Rare's high-speed cartoon beat-'em-up engine
